privateIslands.note: Treat with care: Mexican islands are federal public domain under the Constitution (art. 42, 48) and the Ley General de Bienes Nacionales, so many 'island' listings are private coastal land or concessions. All of them also sit inside the restricted zone (fideicomiso required).

floodZones.label: Mandatory flood insurance purchase (US)
floodZones.value: Required for buildings in a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area (Zones A, AE, AO, AH, V, VE; 1% annual chance flood) when financed by a federally backed or federally regulated lender
floodZones.note: Flood Disaster Protection Act of 1973. A 1% annual chance over a 30-year mortgage is about a 26% chance of at least one flood. Cash buyers are not required to insure.

floodZones.label: UK flood insurance
floodZones.value: No mandatory purchase; Flood Re reinsurance keeps cover affordable for homes built before 1 January 2009
floodZones.note: Homes built from 2009 on are excluded, which pushes new-build flood risk into the price.

floodZones.label: Ireland, Canada and Mexico flood insurance

slopeAndTerrain.note: No primary source gives a per-degree price discount. The mechanic is real: steep ground raises grading, foundation and septic costs and may make a lot unbuildable under local zoning or health codes. Model it as a cost, not an invented price multiplier.

roadAccess.note: No primary source gives a per-cent price effect. The mechanic is legal, not statistical: a lot without legal access (see easements) cannot be financed or built on in most places.

easements.rule: Easements are appurtenant (they run with the land that benefits) or in gross (personal, like a utility line). They are created by express grant, implication, necessity, or prescription. An easement by necessity needs a landlocked parcel that was once under common ownership with the land that cut it off.
Prescriptive period 10 years (CPLR 212(a)). A landlocked owner may petition the town under Highway Law §300 et seq. to lay out a private road, paying damages to the land crossed.
Prescriptive period 15 years (Conn. Gen. Stat. §47-37). No statutory private-road procedure found.
Prescriptive period 5 years (Civil Code §1007; CCP §321). Civil Code §1001 lets a private owner condemn an appurtenant easement for utility service.

Private easements arise by grant, implication (including necessity), or prescription (20 years' use as of right: Prescription Act 1832, lost modern grant). Public rights of way (footpaths, bridleways, byways) are recorded on the council's definitive map under the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 and are highways under the Highways Act 1980. The CROW Act 2000 adds open-access land.

Prescription needs 12 years' use as of right (30 against the State). The Land and Conveyancing Law Reform Act 2021 repealed ss.33-39 of the 2009 Act, so a prescriptive easement no longer has to be registered by court order to exist.

Prescription is 20 years (Real Property Limitations Act s.31), but it cannot run on land in the Land Titles system (Land Titles Act s.51) unless 20 years were complete before conversion. The Road Access Act protects existing access roads from closure.
Easements must be registered. Prescription was abolished (Land Title Act s.24). Access to landlocked land relies on necessity or a registered right of way; statutory rights of way serve utilities.

Servidumbre legal de paso: the owner of an enclosed parcel with no way out to a public road may demand passage over neighboring land, owing only compensation for the harm caused (Código Civil Federal art. 1097; the CDMX and Estado de México civil codes have equivalent provisions).

easementRegistrationCosts.rule: Fixed fee for registering the grant of an easement where no other fee applies

easementRegistrationCosts.note: Which fee applies depends on the application type; read the fee sheet before use.

Not researched to a figure. In Mexico an easement must be in a notarized deed recorded at the Registro Público de la Propiedad, so notary fees dominate.

foreignOwnership.rule: In the restricted zone (100 km from the borders, 50 km from the coasts) foreigners cannot hold direct title to land (Constitution art. 27). They hold residential property through a bank trust (fideicomiso) with a Foreign Affairs (SRE) permit (Ley de Inversión Extranjera arts. 10-11). The trust lasts up to 50 years and is renewable. Outside the zone, foreigners may own directly after signing a Calvo clause waiver (convenio de renuncia) with SRE
foreignOwnership.note: Permission is deemed granted if SRE does not deny it within 5 business days (30 for municipalities partly in the zone). CDMX and most of Estado de México lie outside the zone.

foreignOwnership.rule: SRE fee for a restricted-zone trust permit
foreignOwnership.publisher: Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores (Ley Federal de Derechos art. 25)
foreignOwnership.note: Three different figures surfaced for different years or schedules. Read the current SRE table. Banks also charge trust setup and annual fees.

foreignOwnership.rule: Prohibition on the Purchase of Residential Property by Non-Canadians Act: non-citizens and non-permanent residents may not buy residential property (3 units or fewer, including condos) in census metropolitan areas and agglomerations. Extended to 2027-01-01
foreignOwnership.note: As of 2026-09-30 no further extension has been enacted. The government is reviewing a replacement framework (reported December 2025 to July 2026). Rural land outside CMAs/CAs is exempt.

foreignOwnership.rule: Non-Resident Speculation Tax 25% province-wide on residential purchases by foreign nationals. Toronto adds a 10% municipal NRST from 2025-01-01, 35% combined
foreignOwnership.publisher: Government of Ontario; City of Toronto

foreignOwnership.rule: Additional property transfer tax of 20% on foreign buyers in specified areas. Speculation and Vacancy Tax for foreign owners: 2% through 2025, 3% for 2026, 4% from 2027-01-01
foreignOwnership.note: SVT rates came from a search extract of gov.bc.ca. The 20% APTT was not re-read today.

foreignOwnership.rule: No bar on foreign ownership. Non-resident buyers pay a 2% SDLT surcharge on residential property (since 2021-04-01). Overseas entities must register on the Register of Overseas Entities (Economic Crime Act 2022) before they can register title
No restrictions on foreign ownership of land found

No general federal bar. Foreign persons must report agricultural land holdings to USDA (AFIDA). CFIUS may review purchases near military sites. FIRPTA withholding (generally 15%) applies when a foreign person sells. Many states added 'foreign adversary' farmland limits from 2023; whether NY, CT or CA did was not checked
